plans.name: Current applicable tariff unverified
plans.note: On-demand marketplace has no single stable rate; reserved-commitment quote form requires a minimum 12-month term.

caveats: Unified API to provision GPU instances across providers. Marketplace availability/rates vary by cloud, region, GPU, commitment. No single stable 4/8 or GPU additive price verified. Quote authenticated live catalog before estimating.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.
H100 regime is a dated snapshot of the public marketplace (like Vast); other GPU types are not snapshotted. Billing granularity and minimums depend on the underlying cloud (unverified).

Shadeform is a marketplace/aggregator reselling third-party GPU clouds (Hyperstack, Massed Compute, Scaleway, Lambda, ...); its modes are flagged "sales" (marketplace) and priced only when the user opts in.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Once the instance has entered the 'deleting' status, the account will no longer be billed for the instance.
snapshot_auto.note: Instance status enum is creating / pending_provider / pending / active / error / deleting / deleted: no stopped/sleeping state and no snapshot mechanism in the API.

snapshot_on_demand.note: The full public API (instances create/info/update/delete/restart, clusters, sshkeys, volumes, templates) has no snapshot/image endpoint. Templates are saved launch configurations (image/docker/startup script), not disk or memory snapshots. Underlying clouds may offer snapshots in their own consoles, not through Shadeform.

harness_api.note: GPU marketplace provisioning API only; no agent harness, exec or agent integration documented anywhere in the docs/API.

egress_allowlist.quote: While Shadeform does not currently provide any firewall rules through the platform

egress_http_rules.quote: While Shadeform does not currently provide any firewall rules through the platform

ingress_rules.quote: While Shadeform does not currently provide any firewall rules through the platform
ingress_rules.note: Instances get a public IP; docker launch config uses --network=host with optional port_mappings (host_port -> container_port), which is port remapping, not access control. Underlying-cloud firewalls, if any, are not exposed through Shadeform.

guest_firewall.quote: we can set up a firewall on the GPU instance using Uncomplicated Firewall
guest_firewall.note: Official guide uses sudo ufw on the VM. Does not contain a root agent.

secret_proxy.quote: List of environment variable name and values to automatically add to the instance
secret_proxy.note: Only env vars in the launch configuration (plus registry username/password for docker pulls); no secret store or credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Volumes provide persistent block storage that can be attached to instances for storing data independently of the instance lifecycle.
volume_attach.note: One volume per instance, only at instance creation (volume_ids array of size one), same cloud provider and region only.

isolation.quote: Single-tenant, built for interruption One tenant per node, full GPU passthrough, no overcommitment.
isolation.note: Instances are full VMs (deployment_type: 'vm' in /instances/types) on single-tenant nodes with full GPU passthrough; underlying hypervisor varies per aggregated cloud.

image_oci.quote: Shadeform supports a launch configuration in the Create Instance API that allows you to provide a docker container image and properties. The docker container will be automatically launched on the VM.
image_oci.note: Any accessible Docker/OCI image (with optional registry_credentials) can be launched via docker_configuration.image; not a swappable base VM OS image.

docker_inside.quote: All Shadeform instances come pre-installed with Python, Cuda, and Docker so running containers is easy.

desktop.quote: Shadeform is a single API and platform for deploying and managing cloud GPUs.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (bare GPU VM rental marketplace, no managed GUI/VNC desktop)

browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

captcha_solving.quote: Shadeform is a single API and platform for deploying and managing cloud GPUs.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

egress_ip_type.note: Instances get IPs from the underlying datacenter cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Hyperstack, Massed Compute, etc.); no residential/mobile IP offering documented.

ssh.quote: Please see the Quickstart guide on SSHing into your machine.

snapshot.quote: Once the instance has entered the 'deleting' status, the account will no longer be billed for the instance.
snapshot.note: Instance status enum is creating/pending_provider/pending/active/error/deleting/deleted: no stopped/sleeping state and no disk or memory snapshot endpoint anywhere in the public API.

fork.note: No clone/fork endpoint; Templates only save a launch configuration (image/script/env vars), not a running or disk state to duplicate.

fork_running.note: No fork capability exists at all (see fork).

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No snapshot or fork mechanism exists.

pause_resume.quote: Once the instance has entered the 'deleting' status, the account will no longer be billed for the instance.
pause_resume.note: Instance status lifecycle only has creating/pending/active/error/deleting/deleted -- no 'stopped'/'paused' state to resume from.

wake_on_request.quote: Once the instance has entered the 'deleting' status, the account will no longer be billed for the instance.
wake_on_request.note: There is no stopped/sleeping state, so there is nothing to wake on request.

persistent_disk.quote: Volumes provide persistent block storage that can be attached to instances for storing data independently of the instance lifecycle.
persistent_disk.note: Persistence is via separate attachable volumes, not the VM's own boot disk (there is no stop/start cycle for the boot disk, only create/delete).

volume_shared.quote: supports_multi_mount: Denotes whether the volume supports multiple instances mounting to it at the same time.
volume_shared.note: Support depends on the underlying cloud/volume type; not all volume types support multi-mount.

auto_stop_idle.quote: AutoDelete: Set a date or spend threshold to automatically delete the instance
auto_stop_idle.note: Only an auto-DELETE (date/spend threshold) exists, not an auto-stop/sleep on idle.

live_resize.quote: Update mutable details about the instance. Set a value to null to delete it. Omit a value or leave undefined to keep unchanged.
live_resize.note: UpdateRequest only exposes name, auto_delete, alert, and tags -- no CPU/RAM/GPU resize of a running instance.

agent_harnesses.quote: Shadeform is a single API and platform for deploying and managing cloud GPUs.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no coding-agent templates)

own_agent_api.quote: Shadeform is a single API and platform for deploying and managing cloud GPUs.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (pure GPU instance provisioning API, no browser/computer-use/research agent)

mcp_server.note: No MCP server documented or found in Shadeform's docs/GitHub; only a REST API and OpenAPI spec are offered.

lang_python.quote: All Shadeform instances come pre-installed with Python, Cuda, and Docker so running containers is easy.

lang_node.quote: All Shadeform instances come pre-installed with Python, Cuda, and Docker so running containers is easy.
lang_node.note: Only Python, CUDA and Docker are documented as pre-installed; Node.js is not mentioned (installable yourself via root access, but not out of the box).

public_ipv4.quote: you can take the IP of the instance and go to the following url

inbound_https.note: Ports are reached directly over the instance's raw public IP (plain HTTP shown in docs); no managed HTTPS URL/proxy is provided by Shadeform.

static_egress_ip.note: Each created instance is assigned an IP by the underlying cloud; there is no stop/start of the same instance and no documented fixed/reserved IP feature across instance lifecycles.

windows.note: not offered: os_options observed across instance types are Linux/Ubuntu CUDA images; no Windows option documented.

macos.quote: Shadeform is a single API and platform for deploying and managing cloud GPUs.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (NVIDIA/AMD GPU Linux VM marketplace, no Apple hardware)

self_host.quote: Shadeform is a single API and platform for deploying and managing cloud GPUs.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Shadeform is a hosted SaaS marketplace/aggregator, not installable software.

byoc.quote: If you prefer not to use Shade Cloud, you can also set up cloud access here to have Shadeform manage your own cloud account. Setting up cloud access typically means providing Shadeform with your cloud API key
byoc.note: 'Cloud Access' lets Shadeform provision/manage instances directly inside the customer's own cloud provider account instead of Shadeform's own accounts.

open_source.quote: Shadeform is a single API and platform for deploying and managing cloud GPUs.
open_source.note: No open-source license or public core-product repo found; Shadeform is a closed commercial SaaS platform.

eu_data_residency.note: Aggregated marketplace includes European underlying clouds/regions (per card's regions list and instance region filters), so EU-region instances can be chosen, though this is region selection rather than a formal residency guarantee.

max_session_h.quote: You can query this API on a loop until status changes from pending to active.
max_session_h.note: On-demand VM instances run until explicitly deleted (or an optional auto_delete date/spend threshold is set by the user); no provider-imposed maximum session length is documented. Spot instances can be reclaimed, but that is capacity-based preemption, not a fixed session cap.

arm64.quote: View availability, pricing, and specs for GPU instances across 15+ cloud providers
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Shadeform's entire catalog (gpu_types: B300, GB300, B200, GB200, H200, H100, RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, RTX 4090, A100, L40S, A6000) is NVIDIA data-center/workstation GPU server instances, all on x86 hosts; no ARM CPU/GPU instance type is listed anywhere in the docs or marketplace.

soc2.note: Shadeform's own site footer displays the AICPA SOC badge and links it (and a separate 'Trust center' link) to https://trust.shadeform.com, a Vanta-powered trust center, indicating a SOC 2 report. The trust center itself is access-gated (request-access form) so the exact Type I/II status/report could not be read directly.

hipaa.quote: CCPA GDPR HDS HIPAA ISO 22301 ISO 27001 ISO 27018 ISO 27032 ISO 27701 ISO 27799 PCI DSS PIPEDA SOC 1 Type II SOC 2 Type I SOC 2 Type II SOC 3 Type II
hipaa.note: Shadeform's homepage 'Reserve compute' / capacity-request form lets customers filter/request GPU capacity by compliance certification, and 'HIPAA' is one of the listed options alongside SOC2/ISO27001/etc. This reflects HIPAA-eligible underlying cloud partners sourced through Shadeform's marketplace rather than a Shadeform-signed BAA on its own infrastructure; no explicit 'Shadeform signs a BAA' statement was found.

sso.quote: Log in to Shadeform to continue ... Continue with GitHub Continue with Google
sso.note: The live platform login page offers only email/password, GitHub, and Google sign-in; no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO option is present, and no SSO feature is mentioned anywhere in Shadeform's docs, pricing, or features pages.

cpu_class.quote: Single-tenant, built for interruption. One tenant per node, full GPU passthrough, no overcommitment.
cpu_class.note: Marketplace instances are deployed as single-tenant VMs (deployment_type: 'vm') with 'no overcommitment' per Shadeform's own description of its virtualization/VM layer, implying dedicated (non-shared) vCPUs alongside dedicated GPU passthrough. This statement describes Shadeform's own Flex VM/virtualization layer; exact vCPU allocation policy on resold third-party marketplace listings (Hyperstack, Massed Compute, Lambda, Scaleway, etc.) is set by each underlying cloud and not independently confirmed per listing. 'native' mode has no separate CPU evidence and is omitted.
